q: 1. The nominal shear stress in beams of M 15 grade concrete (even with shear reinforcement) under no circumstances shall exceed ...........
explain: The maximum shear stress (τc max) for M15 grade concrete is 2.5 N/mm² to prevent diagonal compression failure.

q: 2. In a combined footing, the bottom bars under a column should be extended in to the interior of the slab. This distance should be greater of the distance up to the point of contraflexure and ...........
options: 30 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the outer face of the column
42 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the outer face of the column
30 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the inner face of the column
42 times diameter of the main reinforcement from the inner face of the column
explain: Standard detailing rules for development and anchorage require a minimum extension (often 42d for specific steel grades) beyond critical sections.

q: 3. If the allowable punching shear stress is q, the depth of footing from punching shear criterion to carry a load W is given by ...........
explain: This formula relates total load, footing area, column area, and the punching shear perimeter to solve for required depth.

q: 4. In a combined footing if shear stress does not exceed 5 kg/cm², the nominal stirrups provided are ...........
explain: For large combined footings, 8-legged stirrups are often a minimum requirement for nominal shear reinforcement.

q: 5. In a combined footing if shear stress exceed 5 kg/cm², the nominal stirrups provided are ...........
explain: As shear stress increases, more legs are required in the stirrup arrangement to effectively resist the diagonal tension.

q: 6. In a simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed load, the spacing of vertical stumps near supports would be ...........
explain: Shear force is maximum at the supports. To resist this higher shear, stirrups (vertical reinforcement) must be spaced closer together.

q: 7. The ratio of the allowable bond stress in deformed bars to that of plain bars is about ...........
explain: IS 456 allows for a 60% increase (ratio of 1.6) in bond stress for deformed (HYSD) bars compared to plain mild steel bars.

q: 8. According to I.S.: 456 specifications, the safe diagonal tensile stress for M150 grade concrete is ............
explain: Under older metric codes (like M150/M15), the permissible shear stress (which represents diagonal tension) for lower grades of concrete is approximately 5 kg/cm².

q: 9. Dimension of a beam need be changed if the shear stress is more than ............
explain: If the nominal shear stress exceeds the maximum permissible shear stress ($	au_{c,max}$), which is around 20 kg/cm² for M15/M150, the section is unsafe against diagonal compression and dimensions must be increased.

q: 10. The maximum shear stress (q) in concrete of a reinforced cement concrete beam is ............
explain: In the working stress method, the nominal shear stress $q$ is calculated as $V / (b \cdot z)$, where $V$ is shear force, $b$ is width, and $z$ is the lever arm.

q: 11. In a beam the local bond stress $S_b$ is equal to ............
options: shear force / (lever arm × total perimeter of reinforcement)
explain: Local (flexural) bond stress is calculated as $V / (\sum O \cdot j \cdot d)$, where $\sum O$ is the total perimeter of the reinforcement.

q: 12. For M150 mix concrete, according to I.S. specifications, local bond stress, is ............
explain: For an M150 (M15 equivalent) mix, the permissible local bond stress is specifically defined as 10 kg/cm² in the standard tables.

q: 13. If diameter of a reinforcement bar is d, the anchorage value of the hook is ............
explain: A standard U-type hook (180 degree bend) provides an anchorage value equivalent to 16 times the diameter of the bar ($16d$).

q: 14. The radius of a bar bend to form a hook, should not be less than ............
explain: To prevent internal stress concentration and cracking of the steel, the minimum radius for a bend in mild steel is 2 times the bar diameter.

q: 15. The deep beams are designed for ............
explain: According to traditional design rules, deep beams (where span-to-depth ratio is very low) are primarily designed for bending moment, though shear is also a critical check.

q: 16. In a reinforced concrete beam, the shear stress distribution above the neutral axis follows a ............
explain: In the concrete above the neutral axis, the shear stress distribution follows a parabolic curve, similar to a standard homogenous rectangular section.

q: 17. The chances of diagonal tension cracks in R.C.C. member reduce when ............
explain: Axial compression reduces the principal tensile stress, thereby delaying or preventing the formation of diagonal tension cracks.

q: 18. Shear reinforcement is provided in the form of ............
explain: Shear can be resisted using vertical stirrups, bent-up longitudinal bars (inclined bars), or a combination of both.

q: 19. The number of stirrups resisting shear force, in a reinforced beam, is given by ............
explain: The number of stirrups crossing a diagonal crack (roughly at 45 degrees) is determined by the horizontal length of the crack (approx. equal to the lever arm $d$ or $z$) divided by the spacing $s$.

q: 20. A stirrups consists of ............ diameter mild steel bars round the tensile reinforcement.
explain: Stirrups are usually made from smaller diameter bars, typically ranging from 5mm to 12mm.

q: 21. The bond between steel and concrete is mainly due to ............
explain: Bonding is a combination of chemical adhesion, friction between the surfaces, and mechanical interlocking (especially in deformed bars).

q: 22. In the case of deformed bars, the value of bond stress for various grades of concrete is greater by... than the plain bars.
explain: Deformed bars (like HYSD) provide better mechanical interlock than plain bars. Codes allow a 60% increase in design bond stress for deformed bars.

q: 23. When the diameter of a reinforcement bar is φ, the anchorage value of the hook alone is equal to
explain: A standard U-type hook provides an anchorage value equivalent to a straight length of 16 times the diameter (16φ) of the bar.

q: 24. The side face reinforcement, if required, in a T-beam will be
options: 0.2 % to 0.3 % of the web area depending upon the breadth of the slab
explain: When the depth of the web exceeds 750 mm, side face reinforcement is provided at 0.1% of the web area, distributed equally on both faces.

q: 25. The minimum length beyond which at least one-third of the negative moment reinforcement should extend beyond the inflection point is
options: 12 times the diameter of the bar
explain: Reinforcement must extend beyond the theoretical cut-off point by a distance equal to the effective depth or 12 times the bar diameter, whichever is greater.

q: 26. When bars of two different diameters are to be spliced the lap length is calculated on the basis of
options: three-fourths diameter of the larger bar
explain: The lap length is governed by the smaller diameter bar because the force to be transferred is limited by the capacity of the smaller bar.

q: 27. In post-tensioned pre-stressed concrete beam, the end block zone is the zone between the end of the beam and the section where
options: shape of the cross-section of beam
explain: The end block is the region where concentrated anchorage forces disperse into uniform longitudinal stress across the full section (Saint Venant's Principle).

q: 28. The propagation of a shear crack in a pre-stressed concrete member depends upon
options: shape of the cross-section of beam
explain: The shape of the cross-section (like I-beams) significantly influences the distribution of principal stresses and how shear cracks initiate and propagate.

q: 29. An R.C.C. beam not provided with shear reinforcement may develop cracks in its bottom inclined roughly to the horizontal at
explain: Shear stress (diagonal tension) typically acts at a 45-degree angle to the beam axis, which is where cracks initiate if shear reinforcement is absent.

q: 30. In the zone of R.C.C. beam where stress in less than 5 kg/cm², nominal reinforcement is provided at a pitch of
options: one-half lever arm of the section
one-third lever arm of the section
one and half lever arm of the section
explain: Nominal stirrups are typically spaced at a distance equal to the lever arm (or slightly less) to bridge potential 45-degree cracks.
